title: Episode 1 (lines 249–694)

teacherSummary.text: Oedipus defends himself: he acted in self-defence and without knowledge. Ismene brings news that his sons are fighting over Thebes and that an oracle says whoever holds Oedipus' grave will prosper, so Creon is coming for him. Oedipus curses his sons, purifies the grove through Ismene, and answers the elders' questions about the incest and the killing. Theseus arrives, recalls that he too was an exile, and grants Oedipus protection.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Yet am I then / A villain born because in self-defence, / Stricken, I struck the striker back again?” slowly and put it in my own words: Oedipus asks whether he is a villain by nature because, when he was struck, he struck back in self-defence. Next, craft. I notice the repeated sounds of stricken, struck and striker make the act sound like a reflex, not a plan. The strongest word is “villain”: a person evil by nature, which is the charge he rejects. Then, effect. How does Oedipus' question about being a villain change the way he judges his past? My answer: Oedipus' question about being a villain shows him judging his past by intent: in Oedipus Rex he saw only his guilt, but here he argues that a man who acted in self-defence and without knowledge is not a villain (Jebb, 1885/1889, Introduction, § 3).

safeMessaging.teacherScript: In the next part, Oedipus remembers that in his first grief he wanted to die (lines 434–435). Later in the play, the elders sing that it would be best never to have been born (lines 1284–1287), and after their father's death Ismene and Antigone say they wish they could die too (lines 1734–1737, 1778). These are the words of people overwhelmed by loss. The play does not agree with them: Oedipus lives on, wins a home and friends, and is called "blessèd" at his end (line 1764), and his daughters are promised care (lines 1826–1829). In real life, hurting yourself is wrong and is never the answer. If you or someone you know is struggling or thinking about suicide, call or text 988, or chat at 988lifeline.org (988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline), or talk to a school counselor or a trusted adult. You don't have to handle it alone.
